threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: CPython manages memory, so the class is applicable only if a module reaches native memory (ctypes, cffi, a C extension, mmap, the buffer protocol); then the language guarantee ends. Use after free needs a deallocator the program controls; a pure-Python package has none, and ctypes or a C extension is how one would appear.

threats.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary
threats.rationale: CPython manages memory, so the class is applicable only if a module reaches native memory (ctypes, cffi, a C extension, mmap, the buffer protocol); then the language guarantee ends. Python ints are arbitrary precision and cannot wrap; the registry class is the narrow one (wraparound that leads to a wrong buffer size or offset), so it is applicable only if an int is narrowed to a fixed width (struct, array, ctypes, numpy). The size-explosion variant (1 << n, [0] * width) is a different class: python.unbounded-allocation-from-size-argument.

threats.name: Prototype Pollution
threats.rationale: Python has no prototype chain, but the analogous class pollution exists: setattr(OwnClass, k, v), globals()[k] = v or a recursive merge driven by caller keys can reach __class__, __dict__ or a function's __globals__. The v2 subset no_computed_key_writes_to_shared_objects (VER15a section 1.3) gives the class an exclusion route: a live analyzer rule plus a seeded negative-control corpus. The package writes no attribute from caller data by reading.

closed_by.detail: No setattr, __dict__ write, __class__ assignment, object.__setattr__, vars() mutation or recursive merge of caller data into an object.
Python has no prototype chain; the analogous attack (class pollution) needs a write to __class__, __dict__ or an attribute chosen by the attacker. A statement about the language, not a check.

VER15a section 1.3: no write to any class, module, global or metatable object (setattr on a class, globals()[k]), no write under a non-compile-time-constant attribute or key, no recursive merge of caller data. Supersedes the narrower analyzer-rule:py.no-dynamic-attribute-mutation, which stays as a contributing item.

Seeded negative control: planted writes of each shape (setattr on a class, globals()[k]=v, object.__setattr__, recursive merge of caller data), directly and via indirection, and the rule must flag every one.

A class's __name__ is arbitrary text (type("a\nINJECT", (), {}) is legal), so the message can carry newlines or control characters into the caller's logs. Probed on CPython 3.12.13 against main: AND(Cls(), 1) with that class raised TypeError "a must be an int, got a\nINJECT".

closed_by.detail: Rows with a caller type whose __name__ holds a newline or control characters: the exception message must not carry it raw.

No int(), float(), str(), repr(), format(), f-string interpolation or %-format of a caller-supplied value, and no math call on one. Today the error path interpolates the caller int (gates.py:70-71); sizes use int.bit_length (combinational.py:302, 399, 561, 626) and _require_bit_list rebuilds validated bits with int(bit) (combinational.py:94).

threats.name: rebinding module globals and builtins
threats.rationale: Gate functions call each other by module-global name (NAND calls NOT and AND at call time, gates.py:263) and the guard calls builtins type and int by name. Any code in the process can rebind them. Probed on CPython 3.12.13: after logic_gates.gates.AND was replaced, NAND(0, 0) returned 0, a wrong answer. __init__ re-exports hold separate references, so patching one module changes some entry points and not others.

closed_by.detail: Any code in the process can rebind logic_gates.gates.AND, builtins.type or builtins.int; nothing in the language prevents it and nothing in the package can detect it.
